clue.text: The human spirit noted in an Asian capital

indicators.note: the word 'in' tells us the note goes inside the word for the human spirit

parts.note: the soul is the spiritual part of a human being
E is a musical note, so something 'noted' has a note added

explanation.surface: A remark about the human spirit being observed in some Asian capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' reads as 'observed' but supplies the note E, which sits inside SOUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Seoul is the capital city of South Korea, in Asia.

clue.text: One who takes great interest in business

definitions.text: One who takes great interest in business

parts.words: One who takes great interest in business
parts.note: reads as an enthusiastic businessperson, but 'interest' is money charged on a loan, and this lender takes a great deal of it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' means keen attention on the surface and loan charges in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender charging excessive rates of interest is the classic figure meant.

clue.text: Nietzsche's modern-day disciple?

parts.note: the philosopher Nietzsche wrote of the Ubermensch, an ideal higher human; the modern comic-book hero takes that idea's English name

explanation.walkthrough: Nietzsche's Ubermensch is usually translated into English with the very name of the caped comic-strip hero, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic-book hero shares his name with the usual English rendering of Nietzsche's Ubermensch, an ideal higher human.

clue.text: Campaign for a cause America somehow cared about

indicators.note: something done somehow is done in some unspecified way, so these letters are rearranged in no fixed order

explanation.surface: A campaign that America took up because it cared about the cause, in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' shuffles US (America) with CARED; 'about' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusade is a vigorous organised campaign for a cause.

clue.text: Monkey in a box for the lowest outlay

indicators.note: the word 'in' tells us the monkey goes inside the box

parts.note: a chest is a large box
an ape is a kind of monkey in the loose everyday sense

explanation.surface: A monkey kept in a box because it cost the least.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monkey' and 'box' read as a pet in a crate; 'a' is only a link, and the definition is adverbial but the adjective fits 'bought for the lowest outlay'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheapest option is the one costing least money.

clue.text: Good fortune of a person -who is fit

definitions.meaning: a state of health, happiness and prosperity
split in two, 'well' means fit and a 'being' is a person

explanation.walkthrough: The stray hyphen before 'who' is a printing mark. Read as two words, the answer describes a healthy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Welfare and happiness are good fortune; a healthy creature is a 'well' (fit) 'being' (person).

clue.text: Base for crossword compiling used by draughtsmen

definitions.text: Base for crossword compiling used by draughtsmen

parts.words: Base for crossword compiling used by draughtsmen
parts.note: a crossword is set on a square grid; draughtsmen use the triangular drawing instrument of that name

explanation.walkthrough: Setters 'set' crosswords on a square grid; the same two words name a draughtsman's triangular ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangular drawing instrument for right angles, also readable as the square grid a puzzle is set on.

clue.text: The Union game's six-pint men?

parts.note: in rugby union the backs between halves and full-back carry that fractional name

explanation.walkthrough: The Union game is rugby union. Six pints make three-quarters of a gallon, and rugby union's four backs between scrum-half and full-back have that very name.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union, the four backs playing between the halves and the full-back carry this fractional name.

clue.text: Crawler to strike

definitions.meaning: a shell-less garden mollusc that creeps along
to hit hard with the fist

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions side by side: a creeping garden pest and a verb for a heavy punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A slimy garden mollusc creeps slowly; and to hit someone hard is to wallop them.

clue.text: See 8
Open to risk from a libel

indicators.note: the answer is made from these letters, rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone exposed to danger because of a libellous statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' signals that the letters of A LIBEL are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being liable to something means being exposed or subject to it.

clue.text: Study hard for an Olympic medallist

definitions.meaning: to swot intensively before an exam
Steve ..., British middle-distance runner, won 1500m silver at the 1984 Olympics

explanation.walkthrough: Steve Cram is a British runner who won Olympic silver in 1984; 'for' joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise intensively is to swot; and the surname of runner Steve Cram, 1984 Olympic silver winner.

clue.text: Maritime bank the Spanish find of little account poetically

parts.note: Dogger Bank is a large sandbank in the North Sea
el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: Sailors and Spaniards judging a sandbank to be of no poetic worth.
explanation.walkthrough: DOGGER (the North Sea's Dogger Bank) plus EL (Spanish 'the'); 'find' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is trivial, badly made verse, so as an adjective it means poetically worthless.

clue.text: Man of letters in the old days

definitions.text: Man of letters in the old days

parts.words: Man of letters in the old days
parts.note: reads as an old-time author, but means a clerk who once wrote out letters and documents for others

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of letters' usually means a literary figure; here it is a professional copyist.
explanation.definitionFit: Before printing and typing, a professional copyist or clerk wrote documents for others.

clue.text: Pungent solvent produced by expert on pitch

indicators.note: in a down or across charade 'on' places one piece directly against the other

parts.note: an ace is an expert
tone means musical pitch

explanation.surface: An expert at pitch producing a strong-smelling chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: ACE followed by TONE; 'produced by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A volatile, strong-smelling liquid used to dissolve paint and nail varnish.

clue.text: Once a compositor, always a compositor?

definitions.text: Once a compositor, always a compositor?

parts.words: Once a compositor, always a compositor?
parts.note: a compositor sets type, so someone stuck forever in that one role has been 'cast' as a type-setter

explanation.walkthrough: A compositor casts type, and an actor forever given the same role is described with the same two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor confined to one kind of role has been fixed in it; a compositor works with cast metal type.

clue.text: It's 21 that provides one way of putting it

indicators.note: the letters of the two pieces provide the material for a new word when rearranged

parts.note: the answer to clue 21, a smack or sharp taste, is tang

explanation.surface: A cross-reference saying another answer gives one form of expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 21-down is TANG; 'provides' signals that the letters of IT'S and TANG are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Stating something is expressing or saying it, one manner of putting it into words.

clue.text: See 19
Rose may be responsible for this irritation

definitions.text: Rose may be responsible for this irritation

parts.words: Rose may be responsible for this irritation
parts.note: a rose bush has prickles that can lodge in skin, and the phrase for one also means a persistent nuisance

explanation.walkthrough: Literally a prickle from a rose stuck in the skin; figuratively a constant source of annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: A persistent source of annoyance, literally a prickle lodged under the skin.

clue.text: Pluto plot to murder

parts.note: Dis is another name for Pluto, Roman god of the underworld
a patch is a small plot of ground

explanation.surface: A scheme for killing the ruler of the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: DIS (Pluto) plus PATCH (plot of land); 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch someone is to kill them quickly.

clue.text: Smack a backbiter

indicators.note: the first half of 'backbiter' says the biting insect is written backwards

parts.note: a gnat is a small biting insect

explanation.surface: Slapping someone who speaks spitefully behind people's backs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backbiter' looks like a slanderer, but splits into 'back' (reverse) and 'biter' (GNAT), giving TANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a distinctive taste or flavour, as is a sharp tang.

clue.text: German currency for English pound note

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Swapping German money for an English pound note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Currency' means something that flows, a current: the Elbe is a German river. 'For' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a current, and the Elbe flows through Germany.

clue.text: They should show well in a dog-fight at Cruft's

definitions.text: They should show well in a dog-fight at Cruft's

parts.words: They should show well in a dog-fight at Cruft's
parts.note: the breed name of a show dog is also the name for fighters in the ring, so these dogs ought to do well in a fight

explanation.walkthrough: Cruft's is Britain's leading dog show. The dog breed shares its name with prize-fighters, who should shine in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of dog shown at Cruft's, sharing its name with fighters in the ring.

clue.text: One legally bound to be relative

definitions.text: One legally bound to be relative

parts.words: One legally bound to be relative
parts.note: a relative by marriage is tied to the family by law rather than by blood

explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, the answer says 'by law', which is how a relative by marriage is bound.
explanation.definitionFit: A relative by marriage, such as a spouse's parent, is related by legal tie, not blood.

clue.text: Highlight an early warning system

definitions.meaning: a light set high on a hill or tower, read as 'high light'
a signal fire once lit to warn of invasion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Highlight' is read as a light on high, not as a best moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal fire on a hilltop is a light high up, and such fires once gave warning of attack.

clue.text: Drug to take stress off a worker

parts.note: to relax is to ease tension or strain
an ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: Medicine to ease the strain on an employee.
explanation.walkthrough: RELAX plus ANT; 'to' and 'a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A muscle relaxant is a medication that reduces tension.

clue.text: Means a change for a heavenly body

indicators.note: a change in the letters of the first word means they are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that money means a change of fortune for some celestial figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A change' rearranges MEANS; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mensa is a faint southern constellation, the Table Mountain.

clue.text: Currently disturbing to Marie's art

definitions.note: a noun read as 'in current form': the clue uses the adverb loosely for a flow of air

indicators.note: disturbing something throws it into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive S counts here, giving the letters M A R I E S

explanation.surface: Something disturbing to a woman named Marie's artwork at the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbing' rearranges MARIE'S and ART; the S of the possessive is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A current of moving air, such as a wind or draught.
